  • \(\mathrm{cjdeg}_{\varepsilon}(f) \le \mathrm{R}_{\varepsilon}(f)\)
    GLMWZ16 GoosJayram16
    Expand a depth-$d$ randomized tree over its leaves: $\sum_{\ell \text{ labelled } 1} \Pr[\ell]\cdot C_\ell$ is a nonnegative combination of conjunctions of width $\le d$ that $\varepsilon$-approximates $f$. The content of the measure is entirely in the lower bounds.

    The conical junta composition theorem, answering a question of Beame and Lawry. So on the binary AND-OR tree the nonnegative LP already knows the true randomized complexity, up to logarithmic factors.

Lower bounds / separations — there is a family achieving this

  • \(\exists \text{ total search problem } S:\ \mathrm{Q}(S) = 2^{\Omega(\mathrm{cjdeg}(S))}\)
    BenDavidKundu24search
    Strengthens the $\mathrm{Q}$-vs-$\widetilde{\deg}$ separation, since conical junta degree is usually the larger measure. Even a $\mathrm{R}$-vs-$\mathrm{cjdeg}$ separation was not previously known for total search problems.

Total search problems are the query analogue of $\mathsf{TFNP}$: they are "total" in the sense that every input has a valid answer, but they still admit the exponential separations one expects from partial functions. [BenDavidKundu24search] give explicit conversions in both directions between partial functions and total search problems, so the two settings are much closer to each other than either is to total functions.

see also: \(\mathrm{cjdeg}_{\varepsilon}(f)\), \(\mathrm{Q}_{\varepsilon}(f)\), \(\overline{\mathrm{prt}}_{\varepsilon}(f)\), Total functions, partial functions, and relations, [BenDavidKundu24search] data/relations/06-settings.yaml

A single character has sparsity $1$ and $\mathrm{osss} = 1$: the two agree, but neither
grows, so this witnesses no exponent. No function in the zoo has $\mathrm{osss}$ growing
while $\mathrm{spar}$ stays bounded -- indeed $\mathrm{spar}(f) = O(1)$ forces $f$ to be a
constant-size combination of characters, and $\mathrm{osss}$ is then bounded too.
